author: Ella Wales
title: 'Nothing else like it': World of pro fishing descends on Knoxville for Bassmaster Classic - NewsBreak
text:
By Ella Wales ,
7 hours ago
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. ( WATE ) — The Bassmaster Classic is returning to Knoxville for the third time this weekend. The last time the fishing tournament was held in Knoxville was in 2023. On Wednesday, 6 News spoke with a few professional anglers who have competed in past Bassmaster Classics.
Robert Gee, Carl Jocumsen and Ish Monroe all agree on one thing: East Tennessee is the place to be for bass fishing.
“The Tennessee River is very diverse,” Gee said. “We’ve got a very long stretch of river here. We’ve got two lakes, Fort Loudoun and then Tellico Lake.”
Downtown businesses hoping for economic boost from Bassmaster Classic “There’s literally every style of fishing that you can imagine here, and that was a big draw card for me, to be able to learn. It’s like the ultimate training ground for a pro angler,” Jocumsen said.
“Knoxville is definitely in my top five of areas to come and visit throughout the country,” Monroe said.
That’s why Jocumsen moved here in 2019, a few years after coming to the United States from Australia.
“This was actually my first ever Bassmaster Classic that I made three years ago, it was an incredible experience,” he said. “I think nearly 50 Australians flew over for that one and they’re still talking about their Knoxville experience.”
When competitors take off Friday, the first thing they’ll do is pick a spot on the water to start fishing.
Star-studded Pro-Am competition to kick off Bassmaster Classic in Knoxville “Location is everything,” Monroe explained. “If you’re in an area that doesn’t have a lot of fish you’re not going to win. Guys are gonna take their Yamahas, run 70-75 mph for over an hour until they get to a spot, they’re gonna start fishing there.”
Gee said the weather plays into the competition too. The ideal conditions are overcast, so the fish have a harder time seeing the anglers coming.
“Most of them are visual sight feeders, so they like to be in the shade around a little bit darker so they can ambush their prey, because they’re predator fish,” he said.
Gee, a Knoxville native, competed in his first Bassmaster Classic last year in Fort Worth, Texas.
“It’s three days, so you bring your five heaviest fish. If you catch one and it’s bigger than one you already have in your boat, you have to release it back into the water, so your five biggest for three days is going to be the champion on Sunday,” he said.
Winning the Super Bowl of bass fishing is no small feat.
“I have over $3 million in career earnings, I’ve won five Bassmaster events,” Monroe said. “When you win an event, there is nothing else like it.”
▶ See more top stories on WATE.com The competition will begin at 7:45 a.m. at Volunteer Landing on Friday. Weigh-ins will be held each afternoon in Thompson Boling Arena at Food City Center.
